chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The offering of condolences is the Obligation after the burial.
ai.seo_question: When is offering condolences considered obligatory in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the obligation of ta'ziyah (condolences) specifically applies after the burial, distinguishing it from general visits. This ruling underscores the communal duty (fard al-kifaya) to support the bereaved family during the immediate post-burial period, reinforcing social cohesion in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The offering of condolences is the Obligation after the burial’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the necessary condolence should be offered after burial takes place.”
